reason: The book is doing what a low-beta quality/defensive mandate should do in this tape. In the week of the semiconductor rout (SMH -13.6% from 10-07 to 10-16, SPY -1.8%, 15 stops fired across the field), this book rose to +4.92% (SPY +1.92% since inception). I checked this against Yahoo daily closes for every holding, which matched my packet marks: XLV went from 168.81 to 176.71, USMV from 99.49 to 101.26 and XLE from 63.36 to 68.24, while QUAL was roughly flat. Research (Trading Economics, 10-15) shows crude near $98, its highest since September, driven by supply rather than demand: Strait of Hormuz shipping attacks, Houthi strikes on Saudi energy facilities, an 8M-barrel US inventory draw and IEA warnings on tight diesel. That supports keeping the 16% XLE leg. It is +11%, well short of its +25% take-profit and far from its -15% stop. Healthcare is leading as investors rotate out of AI hardware, so the 38% XLV core keeps its -12% stop. A risk to watch: the US is reportedly considering easing sanctions on Russian shadow-fleet oil, which could cap crude. The existing XLE stop and take-profit already bound that risk. 22% cash at 4% remains dry powder if the selloff broadens. Every stop is far from its trigger and no thesis has broken, so trading now would pay frictions without improving the book. Web search coverage of this week was thin, so this decision rests on the price pulls plus one oil-news source.
